materials_digest.description: SEMANTICS A: the digest of the CONTENT of the files the decision's `scope.paths` names. The content is addressed by git blob ids, so the digest changes exactly when a named file's bytes change. The gate computes the same value from the same tree and compares; the producer (`mathc attest-batch`) writes the same value. Per A0 separation (spec/constitution.md §0), this field MUST be non-empty when `kind_` is in `{test, build, observation, analysis}`. An empty value is permitted only when `kind_: review` (a human declaration without a runtime anchor). The kernel emits MC-MATERIALS-DIGEST-EMPTY (Block) for runtime kinds. Loader-side grandfathering for legacy attestations whose `issued_at` predates 2026-10-16 lives in lib/attestations/attestations.ml. The attestation store itself is EXCLUDED from the scope digest: the store is evidence about a scope, not part of it, and including it would make every attestation stale the moment it is committed.

producer.description: Who produced this attestation, and on what runtime anchor. `identity` is class-tagged (`human:` a person, `agent:` a model-driven agent, `ci:` an automated job); the tag is what lets a reader tell a human DECLARATION from a machine OBSERVATION without guessing. `run` names the command whose exit code and output digest produced the attestation, and is REQUIRED whenever a `human:` producer signs a runtime-kind attestation -- a human may declare a review without a runtime anchor, but may not borrow the evidentiary weight of a run they did not name. Per decisions/attestation-producer-vocab-2026-10.

identity.description: Class-tagged producer identity `<class>:<subject>`, with `class` in {human, agent, ci}. The subject may itself contain colons (e.g. `ci:fixture:conformance`, `agent:opencode:ux-3-merge`). An untagged identity asserts nothing about WHO produced the attestation and is rejected (MC-PRODUCER-CLASS-UNDECLARED, Block) on issuance; 62 attestations committed before 2026-10-23 carry untagged identities (`ci-bot`, `dune:test`, `test`, `sub-agent-A4-batchA`, ...) and remain readable by the store loader. A `human:` tag is a DECLARATION, not a proof: the schema cannot verify that a person typed it, so the rule that carries the weight is the one below -- a `human:` producer signing a runtime kind must name the run.

run.description: The command whose exit code and output digest produced this attestation (the `--run` argument of `mathc attest`). Empty is permitted only when `kind_: review` or the producer class is not `human`; see the allOf rule on this schema.

environment_class.description: Free-form environment class string (legacy). Use environment_class_label + environment_class_level for new attestations.

environment_class_level.description: Numeric environment class level 0..4. See spec/algebra-3.2.md §13 and §14 (decisive_threshold).

environment_class_label.description: Coarse environment class label. See spec/algebra-3.2.md §13.

ci_run_id.description: Identifier of the CI run that produced this attestation. Used as input to attestation id derivation. See spec/algebra-3.2.md §13.

substrate_digest.description: sha256 of (kernel version || ocaml version || dependency digests). See spec/algebra-3.2.md §13, §16.

substrate_fingerprint.description: Identifier (𝓢.id) of the substrate declaration this attestation was produced against. See spec/algebra-3.2.md §13, §16.

evidence_digest.description: The digest of what a `--run` command actually produced. This is EVIDENCE, not the materials anchor: `subject.materials_digest` binds the attestation to the content of the decision's scope, while this field records the output of the check that was run. Before semantics A the two were conflated - the run output digest was written into `materials_digest`, where the gate compared it against a digest of changed PATH NAMES - so the two could never be equal and the only attestation the freshness check ever accepted was the one carrying no evidence at all. Empty when no run was executed.

time_observed.description: Optional wall-clock / token-budget / step-count observation closed against a corresponding Decision.time.estimate. Required: scale, value. Optional: observed_at, observed_by. See AGENTS.md §Honest time reporting and bootstrap/time-honesty.yaml.
